title: Plantar Fasciitis and Bone Spurs
claims: AAOS states more than 90% of patients with plantar fasciitis improve within 10 months of starting simple treatment methods.
AAOS describes heel spurs as a result of longstanding tension but notes most people with heel spurs do not have heel pain, and spurs are not the cause of plantar fasciitis pain.
AAOS calls stretching the calves and plantar fascia the most effective way to relieve pain, with a 10-second hold repeated 20 times per foot.
AAOS recommends rolling the foot over a cold water bottle or ice for 20 minutes, 3 to 4 times a day.
AAOS notes night splints stretch the plantar fascia during sleep and are very effective at reducing morning heel pain.
AAOS reserves surgery for people without improvement after 12 months of aggressive nonsurgical treatment.
